text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.46% today as U.S. oil prices held firm at $83.90 a barrel and U.S. refinery utilization stayed elevated at 97.4%, supporting margins for crude processing. The stock has climbed 3.77% over two weeks, tracking a broader recovery in energy stocks tied to geopolitical tensions around Iran—a major oil producer whose exports are now heavily restricted by U.S. Navy blockade operations, tightening global supply.

The tightness in oil markets is real: Iran's crude sales are being squeezed by economic sanctions and military blockade, and global oil stocks remain moderate while U.S. refineries are running near capacity. These conditions support the strong refining margins that companies like Marathon depend on to turn crude into gasoline and diesel profitably.
